name: Editable regions and spellcheck
plain: Makes any element editable; the browser spellcheck may run on what is typed.
meaning: A site can build rich editors from plain HTML. With a cloud assisted spellcheck on, typed text can leave the device, so editing in a web page is not always private.

web.api: contenteditable=true|plaintext-only; spellcheck attribute; document.execCommand (legacy); Selection and Range

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: No iframe flag; designMode on iframes is allowed
steps: Page reads innerHTML and beforeinput events

limits.headline: Can turn parts of a page into a text editor you can type in
limits.user_action: You click into an editable box and start typing
can: Let you type, format and edit text right on the page
Run browser spellcheck on what you type
Send what you type to the site's servers when it chooses to
cannot: Show a permission pop up; there is none
Check spelling in the cloud unless that browser setting is on
See text you type on other pages or in other apps

story.what_it_is: Makes any part of a page editable, with spellcheck that may check what you type.

marketing.name: contenteditable
marketing.pitch: Describes the attribute that makes any element editable, used to build rich text editors.

story.for_you: You click into a block of text on a page and type as if in a word processor. You may see red squiggly lines under typos. If a cloud spellcheck is on, what you type may be sent off your device.
story.for_makers: Makers build rich editors for posts, docs and messages without extra software. Spellcheck is a free feature that keeps users writing instead of leaving.

use_cases.example: An online document editor lets a team type in the same file and see each other's cursors live.
A social post box lets you type, bold and add links before you publish.
A web email composer gives spell check and formatting as you write.
A game's in browser chat box or level editor uses editable text so players can name items and write messages.
A browser code editor uses editable text to show typing, with live feedback.
If cloud spellcheck is on, passwords or secrets typed in an editable region may leave the device.

technical_bounds: execCommand is deprecated but still shipped in all browsers
Spellcheck: Chrome default is on device; Enhanced spell check sends text to Google servers; Edge uses its own service when enabled; Firefox and Safari check locally
Browser extensions (for example grammar tools) can read and change editable regions

abuse: Collecting everything typed into editors (session replay)
Third party spellcheck leakage in cloud mode
